services.summary: We handle the submissions, follow-ups and collections with Dubai government departments so your files keep moving.
services.contentHtml:
What a PRO does for a Dubai business

A company in Dubai deals with several government bodies, and each one has its own portal, forms and approval order. A Public Relations Officer, usually shortened to PRO, is the person who knows which office needs which paper and in what sequence. Our team takes that work off the owner's desk: we prepare the file, check it against the authority's current checklist, submit it, and keep following it until a result is issued.

Transactions we routinely manage

  • Trade licence issue, renewal and amendment through the Department of Economy and Tourism (see trade licence renewal and amendments)
  • Labour transactions through MOHRE and its authorised Tasheel centres (see Amer, Tasheel and Tadbeer facilitation)
  • Residency filings with GDRFA and the ICP (see visa processing and MOHRE application support)
  • Tenancy registration with the Dubai Land Department (see Ejari registration)
  • Municipality and other regulatory approvals (see Dubai Municipality approvals)

How the process works

1. Scope and authority

We list the transactions you need, confirm who is allowed to sign for the company, and agree the fee in writing. If the owner is abroad, a notarised power of attorney or an authorisation letter lets us act on the company's behalf; our POA drafting and attestation service covers that step.

2. Document check

Most delays come from a missing signature, an expired passport copy or a tenancy contract that is not registered. We check every paper before it is submitted, so the file is not rejected on the first day.

3. Submission and tracking

Files are submitted through the authority's online channel or an authorised service centre, and we keep the transaction numbers. You receive a short status message whenever something changes, not only when it finishes.

4. Collection and records

When the licence, permit or certificate is issued we send you the digital copy and file the original. A renewal calendar then tracks expiry dates for your licence, tenancy, labour cards and insurance.

Checklist before you start

  • List every licence, permit and contract that will expire in the next twelve months
  • Confirm who is authorised to sign for the company, and collect valid passport and Emirates ID copies
  • Check that the tenancy registration and trade licence dates are current
  • Decide which transactions you want us to handle and which you will keep in-house
  • Prepare a company authorisation letter or POA if the owner is abroad
  • Agree how you want status updates: email, WhatsApp or a weekly summary

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Waiting until the week of expiry to start a renewal
  • Giving a PRO a general authority with no scope or end date
  • Keeping documents in several inboxes so nobody can find the latest version
  • Paying government fees through several people and losing the receipts

A worked example

For example, a company with two partners abroad and five staff in Dubai has a licence renewal, three visa renewals and an Ejari renewal in the same quarter. A single tracker lists each date, the documents needed and the person who signs, so none of the five filings waits on the others.

Cost and timing

Government fees are paid at the amount the authority charges, and our service fee is shown separately in the quote so you can see exactly what is official. Simple submissions can be completed the same day; transactions that need an inspection or a second department may take days or longer. We give you a realistic window before we begin.

Costs and timings on this page are indicative and were last reviewed in November 2026. Authorities change fees, forms and processing times, so we confirm the current figure in writing before any work starts.

Why owners outsource this work

The cost of a missed expiry date is usually higher than the cost of the service: trade licence and residency delays can block banking, payroll and new contracts. A fixed process, a named case handler and one place to see every transaction is what clients value most. If you want to see how it would work for your company, contact our team and describe the transactions you expect over the next twelve months.

You approve each step, the authority makes the decision, and you receive the result with a clear record.

faqs.question: What does government transactions liaison actually include?
faqs.answer: It covers the full chain around a government file: checking the requirements, preparing and typing the application, submitting it through the right channel, tracking it, paying the official fees, and collecting the result. The authority still makes the decision; we manage the paperwork and the follow-up.

faqs.question: Is a PRO the same as a lawyer or a consultant?
faqs.answer: No. A PRO focuses on procedure: forms, approvals, submissions and renewals. A lawyer gives legal advice and a consultant plans the business structure. We work alongside both, and we will tell you when a question needs legal advice rather than paperwork.

faqs.question: Can I use your team if I live outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. A notarised power of attorney or a company authorisation letter lets us submit and collect on your behalf. Documents signed abroad usually need notarisation and legalisation first, and we explain which steps apply to the country you sign in.

faqs.question: Which Dubai authorities do you deal with most often?
faqs.answer: The Department of Economy and Tourism for licences, MOHRE for labour transactions, GDRFA and the ICP for residency, the Dubai Land Department for tenancy registration, Dubai Municipality for activity approvals and the Dubai Courts notary for attestations.

faqs.question: How do you charge for government fees?
faqs.answer: Official fees are passed through at the amount the authority charges and are listed separately from our professional fee. You see the breakdown before you approve the work, so there is no mixed 'all-in' number to decode.

faqs.question: How long does a typical filing take?
faqs.answer: Straightforward submissions can be completed the same day. Anything that needs an inspection, an external approval or a second department can take days or a few weeks. We give a realistic window at the start and tell you quickly if an authority changes the process.

faqs.question: What happens if a government office rejects the file?
faqs.answer: We read the rejection reason, correct the file and resubmit it. Most rejections come from small errors such as an expired document or a mismatched name spelling, and a pre-submission check removes many of them.

faqs.question: Do you remind us about renewals?
faqs.answer: Yes. We keep a renewal calendar for trade licences, tenancy contracts, labour and residency documents and insurance, and we contact you well before each date so you can avoid late penalties.

faqs.question: I pay in a different currency. Does that complicate things?
faqs.answer: Government fees are charged in UAE dirhams, which are pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725. We invoice in dirhams and can accept bank transfer from abroad; your bank's exchange rate and transfer charges apply on your side.

faqs.question: Will I be able to see what you have submitted for me?
faqs.answer: Yes. You get copies of every submission, the transaction numbers and the final documents, and we keep a record per company so a new manager or accountant can pick up where the last one stopped.

services.title: Dubai Municipality Approvals & Clearance
services.summary: Activity, location and food-safety approvals from Dubai Municipality, prepared and followed up for your business.
services.contentHtml:
When Dubai Municipality approval applies

A trade licence from the Department of Economy and Tourism tells you what a company may do. Some of those activities also need a municipal approval before the business can operate from its premises. The clearest case is food: restaurants, cafés, catering kitchens and food trading usually need a food establishment permit with a review of the location and the facility. Health and safety related activities and certain premises can need further approvals. A company that offers consulting or other desk-based services will often have none to obtain, but the activity list on the licence decides, so it should be checked before you sign a lease.

Two tracks, planned together

The licence and the municipal approval are separate applications. Starting the second one only after the licence is issued is the most common reason a new restaurant opens weeks late. We map both tracks on one timeline: initial approval, tenancy (Ejari registration), municipal review, inspection and final licence. For the licence side, see company formation and business setup.

What the file usually contains

  • Trade licence or initial approval and the activity description
  • Registered tenancy contract and a floor plan or layout for the premises
  • For food activities, a food safety plan (HACCP) and the equipment and menu details the department requests
  • Passport and Emirates ID copies for the owners and the authorised signatory
  • A power of attorney or authorisation letter if we submit for you (POA drafting and attestation)

Inspection and clearance

For premises-based activities an inspector visits to confirm the facility matches the plan and the hygiene and safety rules. We prepare the owner and staff for what is checked, book the visit, and follow up on any remarks so the clearance is not held up by a small correction. Fire safety approval and building permissions are usually handled separately through Civil Defence and the building owner, and we flag them in the same plan.

Checklist before you start

  • Write down the exact activities and menu or product range you plan
  • Confirm the premises address before you pay a deposit
  • Ask the landlord for the building plans and any previous approvals
  • Prepare the layout drawing showing kitchen, storage and customer areas
  • Check whether fire safety and building approvals are needed in parallel
  • Name the person responsible for food safety or compliance in the business

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Signing a lease for premises that cannot pass the inspection
  • Fitting out the kitchen before the layout is approved
  • Describing the activity in the licence differently from the application
  • Forgetting that the licence and municipal approval are separate applications

A worked example

For example, a café owner planning a small kitchen should confirm the layout and extraction before fit-out starts. Approving the drawing first costs days, and re-doing a finished kitchen after an inspection can cost weeks and a lot more.

faqs.question: Does every Dubai business need Dubai Municipality approval?
faqs.answer: No. It depends on the licensed activity and the premises. Food related activities and some health, safety or premises-based activities need it, while many consultancy and online services do not. The activity code on the licence is the starting point for the check.

faqs.question: Is a trade licence enough to start trading?
faqs.answer: Not always. The licence permits the activity, but a regulated activity may need the municipal approval and sometimes a fire safety approval before opening. Check the approval list for your activity before you invest in fit-out.

faqs.question: What is the food safety plan I keep hearing about?
faqs.answer: It is a documented system, commonly based on HACCP, that shows how food is received, stored, prepared and served safely. Food establishment applications normally include it, and it should be kept up to date after approval.

faqs.question: How long does municipal approval take?
faqs.answer: Food activities often take a few weeks when the premises, layout and documents are ready. Delays usually come from incomplete plans, equipment that does not match the application or an inspection that has to be repeated.

faqs.question: What does it cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the activity and premises and published estimates vary widely. We confirm the official fees after reviewing your case and show them separately from our professional fee.

faqs.question: Can I apply before I have a tenancy contract?
faqs.answer: Premises-based approvals usually need a confirmed location, so the lease and its registration normally come first. We can prepare the rest of the file in advance so submission is quick once the address is fixed.

faqs.question: Who handles fire safety approval?
faqs.answer: Fire safety is usually reviewed by Civil Defence and building permissions sit with the building owner or the relevant authority, not with the municipality's food team. We include both in the project plan so nothing is forgotten.

faqs.question: I am setting up from abroad. Can you attend the inspection?
faqs.answer: Yes. With a power of attorney or authorisation letter, our team can receive the inspector, sign the visit report where permitted and follow up on remarks, and we send you photographs and the written outcome.

faqs.question: Are there tax or accounting points I should plan for at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dubai companies also register for corporate tax with the Federal Tax Authority and, above the threshold, for VAT. Corporate tax applies at 9% on taxable income above AED 375,000, and registration is required even where the rate is 0%. Confirm your own position with a tax adviser.

faqs.question: What if the application is refused or corrections are requested?
faqs.answer: We read the remarks, update the plan or documents and resubmit. Most requests are for layout changes, missing certificates or clarifications on the activity, and they are usually solved faster when one person manages the whole file.

services.title: DED / Dubai Economy & Tourism (DET) Services
services.summary: Licence issue, trade name, activity changes and cancellations with the Department of Economy and Tourism, handled start to finish.
services.contentHtml:
What the department does

Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism, known to many business owners by its former name DED, issues and supervises mainland trade licences. Everything that changes the legal identity or permission of a mainland company passes through it: the trade name, the activities, the legal form, the address, the partners and managers, and finally the cancellation. Companies in a free zone are licensed by their own free zone authority and follow that body's rules, not DET's.

Licence types in plain terms

  • Commercial licences cover trading in goods and certain service activities such as logistics.
  • Professional licences cover expertise and services, for example consulting, design or engineering. Some professional activities have extra ownership rules, so we check the activity before you plan the shareholding.
  • Industrial licences cover manufacturing and processing and normally need an industrial premises.

Since the 2021 reforms most mainland activities are open to full foreign ownership, with a limited list of strategic activities still needing a UAE partner or a special approval. Always confirm the current position for your activity. Our company formation service covers the structuring decision in more detail.

Services we file

  • Trade name reservation and initial approval
  • New licence issue after the tenancy is registered (Ejari) and the memorandum is signed (MOA drafting and amendments)
  • Activity addition or removal, change of address, partner or manager
  • Renewal and amendment (trade licence renewal and amendments)
  • Licence cancellation and closing formalities

The process in four steps

1. Requirement check

We compare your activity, ownership and premises with the department's current rules so that the application is built correctly from the start.

2. Documents and approvals

Passports, Emirates IDs where available, the signed memorandum, the registered tenancy and any external approvals are collected. Where another authority must approve the activity first, see our note on Dubai Municipality approvals.

3. Submission

Applications are submitted through the department's online channels. We keep the transaction numbers and answer any request for clarification quickly.

4. Issue and next steps

Once the licence is issued we move on to the immigration card, visas and bank account, where relevant, so the company can start operating without another round of delays.

Checklist before you start

  • Decide the legal form and ownership percentages before choosing the name
  • Write the activity description in plain words and compare it with the licensed activity list
  • Prepare passports and, where available, Emirates IDs for every partner and manager
  • Confirm the premises type your licence category needs
  • Check whether any activity needs another authority's approval first
  • Keep the tenancy, memorandum and licence details identical across all documents

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Choosing a trade name that conflicts with an existing brand
  • Adding an activity without checking its external approvals
  • Changing partners without updating the memorandum first
  • Letting the tenancy registration expire before the licence renewal

A worked example

For example, a consultancy that wants to add training to its licence needs the activity added, and possibly an approval from another body, before it advertises courses. Filing the amendment first avoids a fine for operating outside the licence.

faqs.question: Is DED the same as DET?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Department of Economic Development was renamed the Department of Economy and Tourism. Many forms, documents and conversations still use the older DED name, but the licensing role is the same.

faqs.question: Do free zone companies use DET?
faqs.answer: Generally no. A free zone company is licensed and supervised by its own free zone authority, which has its own forms and fees. A mainland licence from DET is needed to trade directly in the Dubai market without a distributor.

faqs.question: What is the difference between commercial, professional and industrial licences?
faqs.answer: Commercial covers trading in goods and some services, professional covers expertise-based services, and industrial covers manufacturing. The type decides the allowed activities, the premises needed and in some cases the ownership rules.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner own 100% of a Dubai mainland company?
faqs.answer: For most activities, yes, since the 2021 reforms. A limited list of strategic activities still needs a UAE partner or special approval, and some professional activities have extra conditions. We confirm the current rule for your activity before you decide on the structure.

faqs.question: What is initial approval?
faqs.answer: It is the department's first approval of the trade name and activities, given before the tenancy and memorandum are finalised. It tells you the proposed company is acceptable so that you can sign the lease and documents with confidence.

faqs.question: How long does adding an activity take?
faqs.answer: When the activity needs no external approval and the file is complete, it can be done quickly, sometimes within a day. Activities that need another authority's approval take as long as that approval does.

faqs.question: What if my Ejari expires before I renew the licence?
faqs.answer: The tenancy registration normally has to be valid for the licence to be processed, so renew it first. Our service tracks both dates and alerts you in advance. See our page on Ejari registration for the process.

faqs.question: Do I need to be in Dubai to file?
faqs.answer: Not always. With a notarised power of attorney or an authorisation letter, we can submit and collect on your behalf. Some steps, such as signing a memorandum, may need a notary, and we guide you on when.

faqs.question: Are there any tax steps connected to a new licence?
faqs.answer: A newly licensed company should register for corporate tax with the Federal Tax Authority, even if its profit will be inside the 0% band up to AED 375,000, and for VAT once it passes the threshold. We coordinate the timing with your accountant.

faqs.question: Can you cancel a licence and close the company file?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cancellation needs the labour and residency files, the tenancy and bank matters to be settled in the right order. We prepare the closing checklist and submit the cancellation so that no penalty or hold remains on the owners.

services.contentHtml:
What a power of attorney does

A power of attorney, or POA, is a signed authority that allows someone else to act in your name. In Dubai it is used to open or run a company file, sign tenancy and bank documents, handle government transactions, sell or buy assets and appear before authorities. The text decides what the agent may do, so a POA written for one purpose and one period is safer than a general authority with no end date.

Types we draft

  • Special POA for a defined task, such as completing a licence renewal or collecting a certificate
  • General POA for a wider set of company or personal matters, with clear limits
  • Company authorisation letter where the company, not an individual, delegates its authority to a PRO (see government transactions liaison)

How the process works

1. Define the authority

We ask what exactly the agent must do, for how long, and with which limits (for example, no authority to sell property or sign loans). We then draft the text in English and Arabic, because UAE authorities generally require Arabic. Our legal typing and form drafting team prepares the final layout.

2. Sign and notarise

In Dubai a notary public attests the signature. The 2025 fee schedule lists AED 300 per signature attested on an instrument or proxy. Larger or complex documents may involve extra work. Our guide to notary public and legal attestations explains the notary step.

3. Signed outside the UAE

A POA signed abroad normally has to be notarised in the country of signing, legalised or apostilled as that country's rules require, and then attested by the UAE embassy in that country and by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the UAE. The exact chain depends on the country, so we confirm it before you sign anything. For corporate papers, see commercial and corporate document clearing.

4. Delivery and use

You receive the attested original or a certified scan, plus a short note explaining which authorities will accept it and when it expires.

Common mistakes

  • Signing a broad POA when only one transaction is needed
  • Names that differ from the passport or the licence
  • Skipping the Arabic text or translating it informally
  • Forgetting to set an expiry or to revoke a POA that is no longer needed

Checklist before you start

  • Write down exactly what the agent may do and for how long
  • Decide whether the agent can sign alone or only with a second person
  • Check the agent's passport details and spelling of the name
  • Confirm in which country you will sign, so the attestation route is planned first
  • Ask the bank or authority where the POA will be used whether it needs its own wording
  • Plan the Arabic version before the signing appointment

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Signing a very broad POA when one task is needed
  • Forgetting an end date or a way to revoke it
  • Signing abroad before the legalisation route is confirmed
  • Using different name spellings in the POA and the agent's documents

A worked example

For example, an owner who lives abroad authorises a manager only to renew the trade licence and Ejari for one year. The POA lists those two tasks, names the authorities and expires after twelve months, so the owner does not have to worry about its use later.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a general and a special POA?
faqs.answer: A special POA allows a specific task or transaction, such as renewing a licence. A general POA covers a wider set of matters. For company and property affairs a special POA with a clear scope and end date is usually safer.

faqs.question: How much does a notary charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Under the Dubai fee schedule published in 2025, a notary charges AED 300 for each signature attested on an instrument or proxy. Extra translation, drafting and later attestation steps are separate. We confirm the full amount in your quote.

faqs.question: Can I sign a POA for the UAE while I am abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes. You sign before a notary in the country where you are, then the document is legalised or apostilled according to that country's rules and attested by the UAE embassy and the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs. We confirm the exact steps for your country first.

faqs.question: Does the POA have to be in Arabic?
faqs.answer: UAE authorities generally require Arabic or a certified Arabic translation. We draft both versions together so that the English and Arabic text match and the document is accepted without a second round.

faqs.question: How long is a POA valid?
faqs.answer: It is valid for the period stated in the document, or until it is revoked. We recommend setting a clear end date and revoking it formally once the task is done.

faqs.question: Can a PRO or manager use my POA at the bank?
faqs.answer: Banks apply their own rules and may ask for their own form or extra attestation. We check the bank's requirement in advance so the POA is drafted in the form it will accept.

services.contentHtml:
Why the memorandum matters

When partners disagree, when a bank asks who can sign, or when a buyer wants to purchase shares, the Memorandum of Association is the document everyone reads first. A clear MOA lists the shareholders and their percentages, the capital, the manager and signing powers, the licensed activities, the profit and loss sharing, and what happens when a partner wishes to leave. A vague or copied template is a common source of disputes later.

What we draft

  • MOA and articles for a new mainland LLC, tailored to the real ownership and management arrangement
  • Addenda for a change of shareholders or share transfer
  • Capital increase or decrease and change of share distribution
  • Manager or authorised signatory changes, including limits on authority
  • Activity changes aligned with the licence (DET services)

The amendment process

1. Agree the change

The partners confirm what is changing. If one partner is selling, the others normally have a right of first refusal under the MOA, so they should sign or waive it in writing. Skipping that step is a typical reason an amendment stops at the notary.

2. Draft in two languages

We prepare the revised text and the Arabic version. Where partners are abroad, they can sign through a notarised power of attorney (POA drafting) or sign in front of a notary in their own country and have the document legalised (document clearing).

3. Notarise

The signatures are attested by a notary public. The Dubai notary schedule lists AED 300 per signature attested on an instrument, and complex documents may have extra costs. Read our guide to notary public and legal attestations for the notary step.

4. File and update the licence

For a mainland company the notarised document is filed with the licensing authority, and the licence is updated to match. Companies in a free zone file with their own authority. Related bank records, visa files and tenancy details should then be updated, and our trade licence amendment service follows through on those.

Things to decide before you sign

  • Who can sign for the company alone, and above what amount two signatures are needed
  • How shares are valued and transferred on exit, death or dispute
  • Whether the manager is also a shareholder and what happens if the manager leaves
  • How profits are distributed, including any difference between ownership and profit share

Checklist before you start

  • List all shareholders with exact names, nationalities and percentages
  • Decide who manages the company and what the manager may sign alone
  • Agree how profits are shared and how new capital is added
  • Write the rules for selling shares: first refusal, valuation, notice periods
  • Decide what happens if a partner leaves, dies or becomes inactive
  • Check that the activity list matches the licence

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Using a template that does not match the real ownership arrangement
  • Forgetting to update the bank after a shareholder change
  • Leaving out an exit or dispute clause
  • Signing before the other partners have waived or exercised first refusal

A worked example

For example, two partners agree that one will buy out the other over twelve months. The addendum records the price, the payment dates and the date when the manager changes, so the bank and the licensing authority can update their records in the same week.

faqs.question: When do I need to amend the MOA?
faqs.answer: Whenever something it records changes: a shareholder joins or leaves, shares move between partners, capital changes, a manager or signatory changes, or the activity list changes. The amendment is then filed so that the licence and the memorandum match.

services.contentHtml:
Why accurate typing still matters

Many UAE processes still depend on a correctly typed application: a labour contract, a licence amendment, a residency form, a tenancy registration or a letter to an authority. A name that differs from the passport by one letter, or a date in the wrong format, is enough for a rejection. Correct typing at the start saves the owner a second trip and a second fee.

What we prepare

  • Government application forms and attachments for licensing, labour and residency files
  • Commercial contracts, agreements and addenda in English and Arabic
  • Letters, declarations, no-objection certificates and authorisation letters
  • Memoranda and amendments (MOA drafting) and powers of attorney (POA drafting)
  • Translations of supporting documents; for certified translation, see our legal translation service

Our process

1. Source check

We take the original data from passports, Emirates IDs, licences and previous contracts, not from memory or messages. Differences between documents are flagged to you before anything is typed.

2. Drafting and typing

The document is prepared in the format of the destination authority. If it must be bilingual, both versions are prepared together so that numbers, dates and names match line by line.

3. Review

A second person checks the file against the source documents. You also receive a short summary of the facts typed, so that you can confirm them before signature.

4. Submission or hand-over

We either submit the document through the authority's channel (see Amer, Tasheel and Tadbeer services) or hand over the final file for you to sign, notarise or file yourself.

Checklist before you start

  • Gather original passports, Emirates IDs, the licence and the tenancy before typing starts
  • Confirm the exact transaction and which form it needs
  • Check names, dates of birth and passport numbers against the originals
  • Decide whether the document must be in Arabic, English or both
  • Ask who will sign and in what capacity
  • Keep a copy of the final typed version

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Typing from a photo of a document instead of the original
  • Mixing name orders between documents
  • Skipping a second check of numbers and dates
  • Submitting an old form version

For example, a labour contract typed with a passport number that has one digit transposed is rejected a few days later. A second person checking against the passport would have found it before submission.

services.contentHtml:
Mainland, free zone or something else?

The first decision is where the company will be licensed. A mainland company is licensed by the Department of Economy and Tourism and can trade with customers anywhere in the UAE, bid for government work and open offices in the city. A free zone company is licensed by a free zone authority, often with a simple setup and a flexible office, but with limits on trading directly in the mainland market. The right answer depends on who your customers are, what you sell and where your staff will sit. We explain both options in plain language and give a recommendation in writing.

Ownership

Since the 2021 reforms most mainland activities are open to 100% foreign ownership, with a limited list of strategic activities still requiring a UAE partner or special approval. Some professional activities carry extra conditions. Because details change, we confirm the rule for your exact activity before you decide on shares. See also our guide to DED and DET services.

The steps

1. Activity and name

You choose the activity and the proposed trade name. We check the name against the department's naming rules and obtain initial approval.

2. Premises and Ejari

A mainland licence normally needs a registered tenancy contract. Free zones often provide a flexible desk or office as part of the package. Read our page on virtual office and Ejari registration before choosing the address.

3. Memorandum of Association

The partners sign the MOA and, where needed, notarise it (MOA drafting and amendments). Foreign partners can sign through a power of attorney (POA drafting).

4. Approvals and licence

If the activity needs an external approval, such as a municipal approval (Dubai Municipality approvals), it is obtained in parallel. The licence is issued once the approvals, tenancy and memorandum are complete.

5. After the licence

We then handle the immigration card, residence visas (visa processing and MOHRE application support), Emirates ID (Emirates ID and medical fitness), health insurance (corporate and medical insurance) and the supporting documents your bank asks for when opening the account.

Tax at a glance

The UAE applies corporate tax at 9% on taxable income above AED 375,000, with 0% on income up to that amount. Every company, including free zone companies, must register with the Federal Tax Authority, and a small business relief may be available for companies below a revenue limit. Free zone companies can access a 0% rate only on qualifying income and when conditions are met. VAT registration is mandatory once taxable supplies pass the threshold. Confirm your own position with a tax adviser; we coordinate the paperwork with your accountant.

Checklist before you start

  • Decide mainland or free zone based on where your customers are
  • Write the activity description and check ownership rules for it
  • Choose the premises or package and confirm what it supports
  • Decide the number of visas you will need in the first year
  • Prepare passports, proof of address and, for corporate shareholders, attested company documents
  • Plan the bank account documents at the start, not at the end

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Choosing the cheapest package without checking the activity list
  • Signing a lease before the licence type is confirmed
  • Forgetting corporate tax registration after the licence is issued
  • Assuming a free zone licence allows direct trading across the mainland

A worked example

For example, a founder who sells software to UAE businesses would normally compare a mainland professional licence with a free zone licence. The mainland route allows direct invoicing in the market, while the free zone route may suit a team that mainly serves clients abroad.

services.contentHtml:
Why renewal needs planning

An expired trade licence is more than a late fee. It can block visa renewals, payroll files and bank transactions, and it can stop a company from signing new contracts. The renewal depends on other documents being current, especially the tenancy registration, so the steps must be done in the right order. Many advisers recommend starting around 30 to 45 days before expiry to leave room for corrections.

What we need for a renewal

  • The current trade licence
  • A valid registered tenancy contract (Ejari registration)
  • Passport and Emirates ID copies for the owners and manager
  • Any approvals the activity requires (municipal approvals)
  • Signed renewal application, by the owner or through a power of attorney (POA drafting)

Renewal process

1. Review

We check the expiry date, the Ejari date, the activities and the partner details, and flag anything that does not match.

2. Prepare

We prepare the application and supporting documents, then send the draft for your approval with a clear list of the fees.

3. Submit and pay

The renewal is submitted through the authority's online channel, and the fees are paid. Reported processing times range from one to seven working days once the file is complete, but any query from the authority can add time.

4. Collect and update

You receive the renewed licence. We then update the dependent files: labour cards, insurance and the bank.

Amendments

Common amendments include adding or removing an activity, changing the trade name, moving to a new address, adding or removing a partner and appointing a new manager. Partner and manager changes require an updated memorandum (MOA drafting and amendments). New activities may need external approvals, and an address change needs a new tenancy registration. See DED and DET services for the licensing steps.

Penalties and risk

Late renewal can attract penalties and affect related files. Reports about the exact amounts and grace periods vary, so we confirm the current rule for your licence type and avoid guessing. The simplest protection is to renew early.

Checklist before you start

  • Check the expiry date of the licence and of the tenancy registration
  • Collect passports and Emirates IDs for owners and the manager
  • Confirm that the activity list is still correct
  • Check for external approvals that must also be renewed
  • Prepare the signed application or the POA
  • Pay any outstanding fines before submission

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Renewing the licence before the tenancy registration
  • Starting the renewal in the last week
  • Ignoring a change of partner that must be recorded first
  • Not updating the bank and insurance after the licence is renewed

A worked example

For example, a company whose Ejari expires in the same month as its licence renews the tenancy first, receives the new certificate and only then submits the licence renewal. Doing it in the other order usually means a rejected application and a second submission.

services.contentHtml:
What Ejari is

Ejari, meaning "my rent" in Arabic, is the system through which tenancy contracts are registered with the Dubai Land Department. For a business, the Ejari certificate is the proof of the registered business address. Mainland trade licences are normally tied to it, and licence renewals depend on it being current.

Which address options exist?

Mainland: a real, registered lease

A mainland licence generally needs a lease for a premises that fits the activity, registered through Ejari. Industrial activities need suitable facilities, and food and similar activities need premises that can pass municipal checks (Dubai Municipality approvals).

Flexi desk and virtual office

These products give you an address, a desk or a mailing service without a dedicated office. In free zones a flexi desk can satisfy the address requirement for the licence. For mainland licences the position is less clear: advisers report that some professional activities can use a flexi desk where the provider issues an Ejari-compliant lease, while commercial and industrial activities normally need a dedicated unit, and plain virtual office contracts often do not qualify. Because vendors disagree, we check with the licensing authority before you buy.

Free zone office

Free zones usually include an office or desk in the licence package and issue their own lease documents instead of an Ejari.

The Ejari registration process

  1. Prepare the signed tenancy contract with the landlord's details, the property details and the rent.
  2. Collect the landlord's title deed copy, the tenant's passport and Emirates ID or trade licence, and the electricity and water connection details.
  3. Submit the registration online or through an authorised centre, and pay the fee.
  4. Receive the Ejari certificate, which is then used for the licence file (company formation, trade licence renewal).

Checklist before you start

  • Ask the licensing authority what address type your licence accepts
  • Get the landlord's title deed copy and contact details
  • Check the electricity and water connection details of the unit
  • Confirm the lease period and rent in the contract before registration
  • Keep the Ejari certificate with your licence file
  • Add the renewal date to your calendar

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Buying a virtual office for a mainland licence that needs a real lease
  • Registering a contract that the landlord has not signed
  • Letting the Ejari lapse while the licence is still valid
  • Moving offices without amending the licence

A worked example

For example, a consultancy that works from client sites chooses a small shared office with a registered lease for its mainland licence. A free zone consultancy in the same position may only need a flexi desk. Same business, different licence, different address rule.

services.contentHtml:
What "clearing" means in practice

A certificate of incorporation, a board resolution, a power of attorney or financial statements issued in your home country are not automatically accepted in the UAE. Each authority wants proof that the document is genuine and that the signature or seal is real. The proof comes from a chain of attestations, and every link in the chain depends on the one before it.

A typical route for documents coming into the UAE

  1. Notarisation or certified copy in the country of origin, where the document is not already an original public document.
  2. Legalisation or apostille by the competent authority of that country, depending on whether it participates in the apostille system and on how the UAE treats it.
  3. UAE embassy or consulate attestation in that country, where required.
  4. UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation after arrival (MOFA).
  5. Arabic translation by a certified translator, where the receiving authority requires it (legal typing, legal translation).

The exact route varies by country and by document type, so we confirm it before you start. Do not send originals abroad until the route is agreed.

Documents we often clear

  • Certificates of incorporation, good standing and registration extracts
  • Board resolutions, shareholder resolutions and company bylaws
  • Powers of attorney (POA drafting and attestation)
  • Commercial invoices, certificates of origin and contracts
  • Financial statements and bank letters

Documents going out of the UAE

UAE company documents that must be used abroad generally follow a reverse route: notary or authority, Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation and then the foreign embassy or an apostille where available. See also notary public and legal attestations.

Where files go wrong

  • Documents issued too long ago for the receiving authority
  • Names that differ from the passport or the licence
  • Skipping a step because a colleague said it was "not needed" last time
  • Missing translation after attestation

Checklist before you start

  • Identify exactly which documents you need and in which country they were issued
  • Check how old the documents may be for the receiving authority
  • Confirm the attestation chain for that country before ordering originals
  • Check that names match the passport and the licence
  • Plan the Arabic translation after attestation
  • Arrange secure courier for originals

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Sending originals abroad before the route is confirmed
  • Translating a document before it has been attested
  • Ordering a certificate that will be too old when it arrives
  • Skipping a step because it was not needed for a different document

A worked example

For example, a foreign parent company needs a certificate of incorporation and a board resolution for its new Dubai subsidiary. Both go through notarisation, apostille or legalisation, embassy and ministry steps in the same batch, then translation, and arrive together with the licence file.

faqs.question: What is the difference between legalisation and apostille?
faqs.answer: Both prove that a signature or seal on a public document is genuine. An apostille is a single certificate used between countries that joined the Hague Apostille system. Legalisation is the longer chain used where that system does not apply. We confirm which applies for your country.

faqs.question: Do I need embassy attestation for UAE use?
faqs.answer: Often yes for documents coming from abroad, followed by attestation by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The exact route depends on the country and the document, so we confirm it before you begin.

faqs.question: How long does attestation take?
faqs.answer: It depends on the countries involved and the number of steps. Some routes finish within days, others take several weeks. We give an estimate once we know the document and the country.

faqs.question: Do documents need to be translated into Arabic?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for UAE authorities, courts and many banks. Translation is normally done by a certified translator after the document has been attested, so the stamps are translated too.

faqs.question: Can you clear documents from my home country without me travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many steps can be done through courier and local agents, and you may only need to sign before a notary at home. We outline what can be done remotely for your country.

faqs.question: How old can a document be?
faqs.answer: Some authorities want recent certificates, for example a good standing certificate issued within the last few months. We check the requirement of the receiving authority before you order the document.

faqs.question: What if the document has a spelling mistake?
faqs.answer: Correct it at the source before attesting. A mistake that is found after attestation usually means repeating the chain. We check names against the passport and licence before the first step.

faqs.question: Do you handle documents from Asia, Europe and the Americas?
faqs.answer: Yes. The route differs by country, but the logic is the same. We keep a checklist by country and update it when rules change.

faqs.question: How are fees paid, and in what currency?
faqs.answer: Each authority charges in its own currency. We invoice in dirhams and list the authority fees separately. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so dollar transfers are easy to convert.

faqs.question: Can UAE documents be used abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a reverse chain of notary, Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation and, for the foreign destination, an embassy attestation or an apostille where available. We map the steps for each destination country.

services.contentHtml:
Which centre does what

Amer centres

Amer centres accept residency and visa transactions on behalf of the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs in Dubai (GDRFA). Typical tasks include entry permits, status changes, residence visa applications and renewals, and dependents' visas. See visa processing and MOHRE application support and family and visit visa documentation.

Tasheel centres

Tasheel centres are authorised by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) to process private-sector labour transactions: work permits, labour contracts, quota and fee payments, complaints and cancellations. They work with the ministry's systems; the residence side of the process is separate and goes through residency channels.

Tadbeer centres

Tadbeer centres serve households that employ domestic workers, covering recruitment, contracts and permits under the domestic worker framework. They are not used for ordinary company staff.

The order that avoids rejections

  1. Company licence and quota in order (trade licence renewal and amendments)
  2. Labour side: offer or contract and work permit through the labour channel
  3. Entry permit or status change through residency channels
  4. Medical fitness and biometrics (Emirates ID and medical fitness)
  5. Residence visa stamping and Emirates ID
  6. Insurance in place (corporate and medical insurance)

Skipping or reordering these steps is the most common reason for rejection, so we keep a single checklist per employee or dependent.

What we do for you

  • Decide which channel each task belongs to and prepare the file
  • Type and check the data against passports and licences (legal typing)
  • Submit, pay and follow the transaction until a result is issued
  • Collect the documents and update your records (government transactions liaison)

Checklist before you start

  • List the transactions and who they are for (employee, owner, dependent, domestic worker)
  • Check the company's quota and licence validity
  • Collect passports, photos and contracts
  • Confirm the order: labour step, entry or status change, medical, biometrics, visa, ID
  • Check that health insurance is ready
  • Keep every transaction number

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Visiting the wrong centre for a transaction
  • Starting the residency step before the labour step is complete
  • Submitting expired passport copies
  • Losing track of which employee is at which stage

A worked example

For example, a company hiring four people at once keeps a one-page tracker: contract signed, work permit issued, entry permit or status change, medical done, visa stamped, Emirates ID received. Every person is visible at a glance.

What this service is, and what it is not

We provide document preparation, processing and application support only. We do not issue visas or permits: every decision is taken by the relevant UAE authority. We help you assemble a correct, complete file, we process the application through the authorised channels and we support you until the authority has decided.

Files we support

  • Employment-based residence files for new and existing staff
  • Owner, partner and investor residence files linked to a licensed company (company formation)
  • MOHRE steps: work permit, labour contract, fee payments and cancellation (Amer, Tasheel and Tadbeer services)
  • Renewals, status changes and cancellations
  • Dependents' files (family and visit visa documentation)

The usual sequence

1. Company and quota

The employing company must have a valid licence and an establishment record with enough quota for the new hire. We check this first, so you do not discover a quota problem after paying the fees.

2. Labour step

The labour contract and work permit are processed through the MOHRE channel. Our team prepares the offer, the contract data and the supporting documents.

3. Entry or status change

The candidate either enters the UAE on an entry permit or changes status inside the country. We prepare the residency application and the passport and photo requirements.

4. Medical fitness, biometrics and Emirates ID

The employee completes the medical fitness test and biometrics, then the visa is stamped and the Emirates ID is issued. See Emirates ID processing and medical fitness.

5. Insurance and records

Health insurance must be in place (corporate and medical insurance processing), and your HR records are updated.

What makes a file succeed

  • Names, dates and passport numbers identical across all documents
  • Passport validity long enough for the visa period
  • Educational and civil documents attested where the category requires it (document clearing)
  • Applications submitted in the right order

Checklist before you start

  • Confirm the company licence, quota and establishment record
  • Check each candidate's passport validity and photo
  • Decide whether the person enters on an entry permit or changes status inside the UAE
  • Prepare contract data and job title exactly as they should appear
  • Arrange medical fitness and insurance
  • Attest educational documents where the category needs it

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Mismatched job titles between contract and application
  • Passports with too little validity left
  • Skipping a step in the labour or residency sequence
  • Assuming approval is guaranteed

services.contentHtml:
Family residence files

We provide document preparation, processing and application support only. We do not issue visas or permits: every decision is taken by the relevant UAE authority. A resident can apply to sponsor a spouse, children and, in some cases, parents, subject to the sponsor's status, income, accommodation and the category's rules. Salary thresholds have been reported differently by different sources and have changed over time, so we check the authority's current requirement before you pay any fee.

Typical documents

  • Sponsor's passport, residence visa and Emirates ID
  • Marriage certificate, and birth certificates for children, attested for UAE use (document clearing) and translated into Arabic where required (legal translation)
  • A registered tenancy contract or ownership proof for the sponsor's accommodation (Ejari registration)
  • Salary evidence or an employer letter, where the category asks for it
  • Passport copies and photographs for each family member
  • Valid health insurance for dependants (medical insurance processing)

Visit visas

Relatives and business visitors may enter on a visit visa applied for through the authorised channels. The file normally needs the visitor's passport and photo and the sponsor's details, and the entry permit is processed through residency channels. We prepare and check the file and track it, but we cannot promise approval.

How the process runs

1. Eligibility check

We compare the sponsor's status, accommodation and documents with the current category requirements and tell you what is missing before you apply.

2. Attestation and translation

Home-country certificates are attested through the route that applies to the issuing country, then translated. This is often the slowest step, so we start it first.

3. Application

We submit through the authorised channel (Amer and Tasheel services) or help you apply online.

4. Medical, biometrics and Emirates ID

Where residence is granted, family members complete medical fitness and biometrics, and receive Emirates IDs (Emirates ID and medical fitness).

Checklist before you start

  • Confirm the sponsor's residence status and current requirements for the category
  • Check that the sponsor has registered accommodation
  • Gather marriage and birth certificates and plan their attestation
  • Prepare passports and photos for each family member
  • Arrange health insurance for each dependant
  • Plan the medical, biometrics and Emirates ID dates

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Starting the application before the family documents are attested
  • Using documents with spelling differences between family members
  • Assuming the sponsor's old salary evidence is enough
  • Forgetting insurance until the last step

A worked example

For example, a resident wants to bring a spouse and two children. The marriage and birth certificates start attestation first, because that takes longest, while the sponsor's accommodation record, insurance and application are prepared in parallel.

services.contentHtml:
The rule in plain terms

Dubai's health insurance law requires residents to have medical cover, and employers are responsible for providing it to their employees. The basic standard is the Essential Benefits Plan, which sets a minimum level of care. Employers may choose a plan that matches or exceeds it. Dependants such as a spouse and children also need valid cover for their residence files, and in some cases the sponsor pays for it. See the Dubai Health Authority for the framework.

Plan types

  • Essential Benefits Plan: the minimum cover with a limited network and cost sharing
  • Enhanced plans: wider hospital networks, lower co-payments, and optional benefits such as dental, optical or maternity
  • Group corporate plans: one policy for all employees, with options for family members

Premiums depend on the plan, age, gender, family size and network. Some groups, such as elderly parents or women of child-bearing age, can have higher premiums under the schemes' rules.

How we process it

1. Need assessment

We ask how many employees and dependants need cover, their ages, the budget and the hospital network you prefer.

2. Plan comparison

We compare plans from approved insurers on benefits, network, co-payments and exclusions and show the differences in a simple table.

3. Application and policy

Passport, Emirates ID or visa details and the company's information are submitted to the insurer. The policy is issued and linked to the residence file (visa processing and MOHRE application support, Emirates ID and medical fitness).

4. Changes and renewals

New hires, leavers, new dependants and renewals are handled as they happen, and we track expiry dates so that cover does not lapse. Related guidance for staff and families is in our pages on family and visit visa documentation and government transactions liaison.

Penalties and risk

Going without valid cover can lead to fines and may block visa transactions. Published reports on the amounts differ, so we confirm the current position when we assess your case.

Checklist before you start

  • Count employees and dependants and note their ages
  • Decide the minimum plan and any upgrades you want
  • Compare hospital networks near your office and homes
  • Check co-payments, annual limits and exclusions
  • Confirm start dates match the visa timeline
  • Set a reminder for renewal and for leavers and joiners

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Buying the cheapest plan without checking the network
  • Forgetting dependants until a visa application stops
  • Letting cover lapse at renewal
  • Not removing leavers, so the company keeps paying

A worked example

For example, a company of twelve employees compares the basic plan with an enhanced plan. The difference is mostly the network and co-payments, so the comparison table shows hospitals near the office and the cost per employee side by side.

services.contentHtml:
Why approvals get missed

Dubai's regulatory framework is spread across several bodies. A business can hold a valid trade licence and still need a health approval for its premises, a fire safety approval for the fit-out, or a sector permit before it opens. Discovering one of them late is the most expensive way to find out. A short mapping exercise at the start of a project removes that risk.

What we map for you

  • Licence and activity with the licensing authority (DED and DET services)
  • Municipality approvals for activities and premises (Dubai Municipality approvals)
  • Health sector approvals through the Dubai Health Authority where the activity is medical
  • Fire and building safety approvals through the relevant bodies and the landlord
  • Sector regulators for regulated activities such as finance, education and others, each with its own permit process
  • Labour and residency for the people who will work in the business (visa processing support)

Our method

1. Project brief

We record the activity, the premises, the number of staff, the start date and any special features such as food handling, medical equipment or public access.

2. Authority map

We produce a list of authorities and approvals in the order they must be obtained, with the documents needed for each and the time expected.

3. Submission and tracking

We prepare and submit each application (government transactions liaison), track the answers and handle queries.

4. Close-out file

When all clearances are in, you receive a single file with every approval and its expiry date, and we add the dates to the renewal calendar.

No-objection certificates

A no-objection certificate, or NOC, is a letter from an employer, landlord, partner or authority stating that it has no objection to a specific action. They are often required for transfers, changes of activity or premises, and some visa steps. We draft the request, obtain the NOC and make sure its wording matches what the receiving authority expects (legal typing and form drafting).

Checklist before you start

  • Describe the project: activity, premises, staff and start date
  • Ask which authorities regulate the activity
  • List what must be approved before opening, and what can follow
  • Collect the documents each authority asks for
  • Plan inspections and the time between them
  • Keep one file with every approval and its expiry

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Discovering a missing approval after the fit-out is done
  • Assuming one approval covers all authorities
  • Submitting applications in the wrong order
  • Letting an approval expire unnoticed

A worked example

For example, a clinic needs a health-sector approval as well as its trade licence and premises approvals. Listing them at the start shows that the health approval has the longest lead time, so it is started first.

services.contentHtml:
What a notary does

A notary public confirms the identity of the people signing, checks that they understand and sign the document voluntarily, and attests the signature. The result is a document that authorities, banks and courts treat as genuine. Typical documents include powers of attorney (POA drafting and attestation), agreements, declarations, affidavits, share transfers and memorandum amendments (MOA drafting and amendments).

Fees

Dubai's notary fee schedule, amended by Executive Council Resolution No. (72) of 2025, lists AED 300 per signature attested on an instrument or proxy. Private notaries collect fees under a separate schedule. Translation, drafting and the later attestation steps are additional. Please confirm the current schedule before relying on any figure; we do this for you at quotation.

Before you go to the notary

  • Valid passports or Emirates IDs for everyone who signs, with names that match the document
  • The final text, in Arabic or with a certified Arabic translation (legal typing and form drafting)
  • Company documents if a company signs, and proof of the signatory's authority
  • Supporting papers, such as a licence or a title deed, where the document refers to them

After the notary

For use inside the UAE the notarised document is usually enough. For use in another country the next steps typically include attestation by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) and then an embassy attestation or, where available, an apostille. For documents arriving from abroad the chain runs in the other direction, as explained in our guide to commercial and corporate document clearing.

How we help

1. Review and draft

We check your document for clarity, names and numbers, and draft it where you do not have one.

2. Translation and formatting

We produce the Arabic text and format the document the way the notary and the receiving authority expect.

3. Appointment and signing

We book the appointment, explain who must attend with which documents, and assist at the notary where permitted.

4. Onward attestation

We arrange the remaining steps and deliver the final document, or a certified copy, to you.

Checklist before you start

  • Prepare the final document and read it carefully
  • Confirm who must sign and in what capacity
  • Check passports or Emirates IDs for everyone who signs
  • Plan the Arabic text or certified translation
  • Ask where the document will be used and whether more attestation is needed
  • Keep a certified copy

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Going to the notary before the text is final
  • Signing with an old signature or an expired ID
  • Skipping the Ministry of Foreign Affairs step for use abroad
  • Using a document with blank spaces

A worked example

For example, a share transfer agreement is signed in front of a notary, then filed with the licensing authority. The same agreement, if it must be used in another country, continues to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the destination country's embassy or apostille route.

The Emirates ID in the residence process

The Emirates ID is the identity card issued to UAE residents. It links to the residence visa and is used for banking, health insurance, tenancy, driving and many government services. It is applied for as part of the residence process, after entry or status change, medical fitness and biometrics. Our pages on visa processing support and family and visit visa documentation show where it sits in the sequence.

Medical fitness

A mandatory medical fitness test, done at an approved centre, is a prerequisite for most residence categories. It usually includes a blood test and a chest X-ray, and the result is sent electronically to the authority. Reported costs range from a few hundred dirhams to more, depending on the clinic and the package, and some centres offer faster service for an extra charge. If a result is flagged, the authority tells the applicant what to do next.

The steps

1. Prepare the file

We prepare the entry or status change application and the passport and photo files (Amer, Tasheel and Tadbeer services).

2. Book the medical test

We choose an approved centre close to the applicant, book the slot and explain what to bring: passport, entry permit or visa details and, where required, a photograph.

3. Biometrics and application

Fingerprints, a photo and signature are captured at an authorised centre, and the Emirates ID application is typed and submitted (legal typing).

4. Visa stamping and ID issue

Once the visa is processed and the ID is printed, it is delivered to the registered address or collected. We track the status until you receive it.

5. Updates

If your ID or residence details change, for example a new job, new address or renewal, we handle the updates so that records stay consistent.

Insurance and tenancy

The residence file also needs valid health insurance (corporate and medical insurance processing), and families need a registered tenancy (Ejari registration). We confirm these items before the application, so nothing stops the file at the last step.

Checklist before you start

  • Confirm whether the entry permit or status change is complete
  • Book the medical fitness test and note what to bring
  • Check passport validity and photo quality
  • Make sure health insurance is in place
  • Plan the biometrics visit
  • Keep the application number until the card arrives

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Booking the ID before the visa step is ready
  • Missing the biometrics appointment
  • Using a photo that does not meet the requirements
  • Forgetting to update the ID after a job change

A worked example

For example, a new hire lands on Sunday, completes the medical test on Monday, gives biometrics on Tuesday and has the visa stamped later that week. Booking all appointments up front avoids days of waiting between steps.

faqs.question: What is the Emirates ID?
faqs.answer: It is the identity card issued to UAE residents. It links to the residence visa and is used for banking, insurance, tenancy, driving and many government services.

faqs.question: Is the medical fitness test mandatory?
faqs.answer: For most residence categories, yes. It is done at an approved centre, usually with a blood test and chest X-ray, and the result is sent to the authority electronically.

faqs.question: How much does the Emirates ID cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the validity period and have changed in recent years, and a centre's service charge is added. We confirm the current total for your case before you pay.

faqs.question: How much does the medical test cost?
faqs.answer: Reported figures range from a few hundred dirhams to more, depending on the clinic and whether you choose faster service. We quote the actual price at booking.

faqs.question: In what order do these steps happen?
faqs.answer: Typically entry permit or status change first, then medical fitness, biometrics, visa stamping and finally the Emirates ID. Some steps can overlap, and we keep the order on one checklist.

faqs.question: How long does it take to receive the ID?
faqs.answer: It depends on the authority and the file. Booking the appointments is quick, and the ID is delivered after processing. We track it and tell you when to expect it.

faqs.question: What if the medical test result is not clear?
faqs.answer: The authority informs the applicant and explains the next step, which may be a repeat test or further review. We help you follow the instructions and update the file.

faqs.question: Do children and family members need the same steps?
faqs.answer: Dependants generally follow a similar process, with medical fitness, biometrics and an Emirates ID, subject to age rules. See our page on family and visit visa documentation.

faqs.question: Can I renew my Emirates ID with you?
faqs.answer: Yes. We prepare renewals, book biometrics where needed and keep the dates in our reminder calendar so that the ID and the visa do not expire at different times.

faqs.question: What about payment from abroad?
faqs.answer: Fees are charged in dirhams, pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725. Payments from abroad are accepted by bank transfer, and your bank's exchange rate and charges apply for other currencies.
